topic: Failure of unrestricted surjectivity for pseudo-Frobenius row-deletion symmetrization
title: A negative answer to Delgado, Süer and Yeşil's symmetrization question

creators.name: Wenlin Zhang
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: The surjectivity question in the final paragraph of Section 5, p. 9, of Delgado, Süer and Yeşil's A Symmetrization for Almost Symmetric Numerical Semigroups (arXiv:2611.14268v1) has a negative answer: pseudo-Frobenius row deletion always leaves 1 as a gap. The symmetric numerical set {0,1} union {n >= 4} is therefore not in the image. In fact, at least half of all symmetric numerical sets with any prescribed odd Frobenius number at least 3 are excluded. Every symmetric numerical semigroup, in contrast, is fixed by the map. We identify the entire fiber over the target with sole gap 1 and obtain at most 2^(floor((F+1)/2)-1) distinct images of sources with Frobenius number F.
summary: Pseudo-Frobenius row deletion on every proper numerical semigroup omits 1, excluding the symmetric target with gaps {2,3} and half the targets at every odd Frobenius number at least 3. The symmetric numerical semigroups are exactly the fixed points among semigroups. The fiber over the target with sole gap 1 consists exactly of the ordinary semigroups, one per positive source Frobenius number. For fixed source Frobenius F, the number of distinct images is at most 2^(floor((F+1)/2)-1). The target-count ingredient is credited to Marzuola–Miller, and the reduced-diagram correspondence to Süer–Yeşil. Exact finite checks cover all 1,654 proper numerical semigroups with Frobenius number at most 18, including 367 almost symmetric sources, and reproduce the first 18 rows of the posing paper's Table 1.
